issues.description: Constructor mismatch for class Bitmap24: the template header (example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp in the TEMPLATE_REPOSITORY) declares a three-parameter constructor Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height, int depth), while the template implementation (example_program/src/Bitmap24.cpp in the TEMPLATE_REPOSITORY) defines Bitmap24::Bitmap24(int p_width, int p_height) (two parameters). The solution header (example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp in the SOLUTION_REPOSITORY) and the implementation use a two-parameter constructor Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height). This inconsistency will cause compilation errors and confuses students which constructor signature to implement/use.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor signatures consistent. Preferred fix: update the template header example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp to declare Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height) (remove the unused 'depth' parameter) so it matches the implementation in Bitmap24.cpp and the solution. Alternatively, implement a matching three-parameter constructor in Bitmap24.cpp and update the solution accordingly if the 'depth' parameter is required, but removing the extra parameter is recommended since the example implementation and solution use two parameters.

issues.description: The Bitmap24 constructor is declared with a different parameter list in the template header than it is implemented and than in the solution header. In template/example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp the class declares Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height, int depth); while the template implementation in example_program/src/Bitmap24.cpp defines Bitmap24::Bitmap24(int p_width, int p_height) (two parameters). The solution header (solution_repository/example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp) declares Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height);. This mismatch (three-arg declaration vs two-arg definition and solution) prevents students from mapping the header declaration to the implementation and can cause compilation errors or confusion about which constructor to implement or call.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor signature consistent across header and implementation. Prefer aligning the template header with the implementation/solution by changing the declaration in example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp to: Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height);. Alternatively, if the extra 'depth' parameter is intended, add and implement a matching three-argument constructor in example_program/src/Bitmap24.cpp and update the solution accordingly. Ensure both template and solution use the same two-argument signature to avoid compilation errors and reduce student confusion.
